entry.title: Bangladesh: Withholding tax return filed quarterly instead of monthly
entry.summary: The Finance Ordinance 2025, issued with effect from 1 July 2025, requires the withholding income tax return to be submitted quarterly instead of monthly. The deadline is the 25th of the month following the end of each quarter, with no option for time extensions.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2025

The Finance Ordinance 2025, issued with effect from 1 July 2025, requires the withholding income tax return to be submitted quarterly instead of monthly. The deadline is the 25th of the month following the end of each quarter, with no option for time extensions.

For the employer:

  • File the withholding income tax return once per quarter, by the 25th of the month after quarter-end, instead of monthly.
  • Reconcile tax withheld across the quarter before filing, since no time extension is available.

Source: KPMG Bangladesh - Salient features of Finance Ordinance 2025

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Costa Rica: CCSS pension (IVM) contributions rise: employer 5.58%, employee 4.33%
entry.summary: From 1 January 2026 the CCSS Invalidity, Old Age and Death (IVM) contributions rise under the gradual 1.00% increase every 3 years in Transitory XI of the IVM Regulation: employer 5.42% to 5.58% and employee 4.17% to 4.33%, with the state contribution at 1.75% (total IVM…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026 · Scheduled step, planned to 31 Dec 2028

From 1 January 2026 the CCSS Invalidity, Old Age and Death (IVM) contributions rise under the gradual 1.00% increase every 3 years in Transitory XI of the IVM Regulation: employer 5.42% to 5.58% and employee 4.17% to 4.33%, with the state contribution at 1.75% (total IVM 11.66%). Total employer charges become 26.83% and total employee charges 10.83% (37.66% combined), with the rates planned to apply until 31 December 2028.

For the employer:

  • Apply the new IVM rates from the first pay period of 2026; the other components of the employer-employee contributions are unchanged.
  • Update payroll to total employer charges of 26.83% of gross salary.

Source: EY Central America - Costa Rica: aumento en cuotas obrero patronales aplicable desde enero 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Costa Rica: 2026 salary tax bands: exempt up to CRC 918,000 a month
entry.summary: Executive Decree No. 45333-H (La Gaceta No. 229, 5 December 2025) sets the 2026 income tax bands for employees: 0% up to CRC 918,000 (CRC 922,000 in 2025), 10% above that up to CRC 1,347,000, 15% up to CRC 2,364,000, 20% up to CRC 4,727,000 and 25% above. The monthly tax…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026

Executive Decree No. 45333-H (La Gaceta No. 229, 5 December 2025) sets the 2026 income tax bands for employees: 0% up to CRC 918,000 (CRC 922,000 in 2025), 10% above that up to CRC 1,347,000, 15% up to CRC 2,364,000, 20% up to CRC 4,727,000 and 25% above. The monthly tax credits are CRC 1,710 per child and CRC 2,590 for a spouse.

For the employer:

  • Load the 2026 bands and credits into salary tax withholding from January 2026.
  • Apply the CRC 1,710 per-child and CRC 2,590 spouse credits where the employee claims them.

Source: EY Central America - Costa Rica: Ministerio de Hacienda estableció los tramos del impuesto sobre la renta para el periodo fiscal 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.content:
In force, Jan 2026 · Annual filing

The Tax Service (SRI) reminded employers, individuals and companies, that the Anexo de Retenciones en la Fuente bajo Relación de Dependencia for fiscal year 2025 must be filed by 7 February 2026, with the date set by the ninth digit of the RUC.

entry.title: Estonia: Second-pillar pension contribution of 2%, 4% or 6% applies from 2025
entry.summary: Since 1 January 2025 employees in the funded pension (II pillar) can choose a contribution rate of 2%, 4% or 6%; the default stays 2% unless the person applies to the registrar for a higher rate. The employer withholds whatever rate the Funded Pension Registry shows.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2025

Since 1 January 2025 employees in the funded pension (II pillar) can choose a contribution rate of 2%, 4% or 6%; the default stays 2% unless the person applies to the registrar for a higher rate. The employer withholds whatever rate the Funded Pension Registry shows.

For the employer:

  • Withhold the 2%, 4% or 6% funded pension contribution according to the Funded Pension Registry data for each employee.
  • Check the withholding obligation before payroll in December, April and August, since it can change on 1 January, 1 May and 1 September.

Source: Tax and Customs Board (EMTA) - Tax rates

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Estonia: Minimum monthly social tax base rises to €886 for 2026
entry.summary: For 2026 the Tax and Customs Board states that the minimum monthly social tax obligation is based on €886 (up from €820 in 2025), so the minimum social tax is €292.38 per month at the 33% rate.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026

For 2026 the Tax and Customs Board states that the minimum monthly social tax obligation is based on €886 (up from €820 in 2025), so the minimum social tax is €292.38 per month at the 33% rate.

For the employer:

  • Pay at least €292.38 of social tax per month for each employee in 2026, even if the wage paid is below €886.
  • Keep the 33% social tax rate and 1.6%/0.8% unemployment insurance rates for 2026 payroll (unchanged from 2025).

Source: Tax and Customs Board (EMTA) - Tax rates

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.content:
In force, 1 Sep 2026

GRA says the Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act 1178) took effect on 1 September 2026 and published new monthly PAYE bands for resident individuals: first GHS 588 at 0%, then 5%, 10%, 17.5%, 25%, 30% and 35% on income above GHS 50,000 a month.

entry.title: Kuwait: Central Bank launches Kuwait Wage Payment System (KWPS) for private-sector wages
entry.summary: On 28 September 2026 the Central Bank of Kuwait (CBK) announced the launch of the Kuwait Wage Payment System (KWPS), a national platform for processing and monitoring wage transfers for private-sector employees through local banks so that wages are disbursed electronically. CBK…
entry.content:
In force, 28 Sep 2026

On 28 September 2026 the Central Bank of Kuwait (CBK) announced the launch of the Kuwait Wage Payment System (KWPS), a national platform for processing and monitoring wage transfers for private-sector employees through local banks so that wages are disbursed electronically. CBK manages the system technically and operationally, while the Public Authority for Manpower oversees employers' compliance with the KWPS provisions.

For the employer:

  • Expect private-sector wage transfers to be processed and monitored through the KWPS via local banks; ask your bank and the Public Authority for Manpower how your payroll file must be submitted.
  • The system lets supervisory authorities monitor wage disbursement in real time and detect non-compliance early, so late or missing wage payments become visible to the regulator.

Source: Central Bank of Kuwait - CBK Launches Kuwait Wage Payment System (KWPS)

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Qatar: Qatar Labour Law amended: Ministry can suspend services of employers over wage violations
entry.summary: Law No. 9 of 2026 (dated 11 June 2026, published in Official Gazette No. 11 on 25 June 2026) amends the Labour Law (Law No. 14 of 2004). New Article 146 bis lets the Minister of Labour suspend all or some of an employer's applications and transactions with the Ministry for a…
entry.content:
In force, 25 Jun 2026

Law No. 9 of 2026 (dated 11 June 2026, published in Official Gazette No. 11 on 25 June 2026) amends the Labour Law (Law No. 14 of 2004). New Article 146 bis lets the Minister of Labour suspend all or some of an employer's applications and transactions with the Ministry for a breach of the law, and extend the suspension to the employer's related establishments where the breach is repeated in the same year or collective disputes arise from late payment of wages. A worker harmed by a breach of Article 66 (reported by law firms as the wage-payment provision) may ask to change employer or end the contract, with the employer bearing the cost of return to the worker's home country.

For the employer:

  • Pay wages on time: late wages in a collective dispute can lead to suspension of Ministry of Labour transactions, extended to related establishments.
  • The suspension does not cover attestation of employment contracts or renewal of work licences and residence permits of the workers of the establishments concerned.
  • Under new Article 146 bis/1 the Minister may publish the names of establishments that repeatedly breach certain provisions, including Article 66.

Source: Al Meezan (Qatar Legal Portal) - Law No. 9 of 2026 amending the Labour Law

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Uganda: Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026: PAYE tax-free threshold rises to UGX 335,000 a month
entry.summary: The Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026, assented to on 20 August 2026, applies from 1 July 2026 and raises the resident-individual tax-free threshold from UGX 2,820,000 to UGX 4,020,000 a year (UGX 235,000 to UGX 335,000 a month) and adds a 25% band before the 30% rate.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

The Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026, assented to on 20 August 2026, applies from 1 July 2026 and raises the resident-individual tax-free threshold from UGX 2,820,000 to UGX 4,020,000 a year (UGX 235,000 to UGX 335,000 a month) and adds a 25% band before the 30% rate.

For the employer:

  • Apply the new annual scale: nil to UGX 4,020,000; 20% to UGX 4,920,000; UGX 180,000 plus 25% to UGX 5,820,000; UGX 405,000 plus 30% above that; plus 10% on income over UGX 120,000,000.
  • Re-run July and August 2026 payroll on the new bands and reconcile any over-withheld PAYE with the Uganda Revenue Authority.

Source: Kampala Associated Advocates - KAA Tax Alert: Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Belgium: GMMI indexed to €2,233.61 from 1 July 2026
entry.summary: On 1 July 2026 the guaranteed average minimum monthly income (GMMI) is indexed after the pivot index was exceeded at the end of June 2026, raising it from €2,189.81 (base amount from 1 April 2026) to €2,233.61 a month for workers aged 18 and over.
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

On 1 July 2026 the guaranteed average minimum monthly income (GMMI) is indexed after the pivot index was exceeded at the end of June 2026, raising it from €2,189.81 (base amount from 1 April 2026) to €2,233.61 a month for workers aged 18 and over.

For the employer:

  • Raise any employee aged 18+ paid at or near the GMMI to at least €2,233.61 a month from 1 July 2026, and correct the July 2026 pay run if it was processed at the old amount.

Source: Nationale Arbeidsraad (NAR) - Tabel cao-bedragen bijgewerkt op 01.07.2026 (cao nr. 43/18)

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Finland: State tax scale indexed, top marginal rate cut to 52%, earned-income credit raised
entry.summary: For 2026 the lower thresholds of the state income tax scale were indexed by about 3.5%, and the top marginal tax rate was lowered to 52% (previously about 59%); this is the overall marginal rate as stated by Vero, not the state scale's top band (37.50%, before municipal and…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026

For 2026 the lower thresholds of the state income tax scale were indexed by about 3.5%, and the top marginal tax rate was lowered to 52% (previously about 59%); this is the overall marginal rate as stated by Vero, not the state scale's top band (37.50%, before municipal and church tax). The maximum earned-income tax credit (työtulovähennys) rose by €205 to €3,430, and its child supplement rose by €55 to €105 per child.

For the employer:

  • Withholding is driven by each employee's tax card - make sure 2026 tax cards from Vero are loaded for the first 2026 pay run.

Source: Vero (Finnish Tax Administration) - Muutokset veroperusteisiin 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Spain: SMI rises 3.1% to €1,221 a month, payable from 1 January 2026
entry.summary: Royal Decree 126/2026 sets the Spanish minimum wage (SMI) for 2026 at €1,221 a month or €40.70 a day, 3.1% more than in 2025. In annual terms the SMI is never taken as less than €17,094. The decree came into force on 20 February 2026 and the SMI is payable with effect from 1…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026 · Effective 1 Jan 2026 (retroactive)

Royal Decree 126/2026 sets the Spanish minimum wage (SMI) for 2026 at €1,221 a month or €40.70 a day, 3.1% more than in 2025. In annual terms the SMI is never taken as less than €17,094. The decree came into force on 20 February 2026 and the SMI is payable with effect from 1 January 2026.

For the employer:

  • Pay at least €1,221 a month (or €40.70 a day, if pay is set by the day) for the full legal working time, and pro rata for shorter hours, with effect from 1 January 2026.
  • Compare annual pay with the SMI plus the salary supplements named in article 2, never taking less than €17,094. Pay that falls below that annual total must be raised to it (article 3).
  • Workers hired for up to 120 days by the same employer: minimum €57.82 per working day. Domestic workers paid by the hour: €9.55 per hour worked.

Source: BOE - Real Decreto 126/2026, por el que se fija el salario mínimo interprofesional para 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Oman: Mandatory performance-based annual increments for Omani private-sector workers
entry.summary: Oman's Ministerial Resolution 317/2025 sets a minimum periodic increment for Omani workers in the private sector, paid annually on 1 January based on performance (the resolution has been in force since 28 July 2025; the first increments are due on 1 January 2026): 5% of basic…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026 · Ministerial Resolution 317/2025

Oman's Ministerial Resolution 317/2025 sets a minimum periodic increment for Omani workers in the private sector, paid annually on 1 January based on performance (the resolution has been in force since 28 July 2025; the first increments are due on 1 January 2026): 5% of basic salary for excellent, 4% very good, 3% good, 2% acceptable, and no increment for poor. Workers must have been appointed for at least six months in the establishment.

For the employer:

  • Award the minimum increment (2-5% of basic salary by rating) to eligible Omani workers each 1 January.
  • Complete performance evaluations before the increment date.
  • An administrative fine of RO 50 applies per violation, multiplied by the number of workers involved.

Source: Oman Observer - Minimum periodic increment for Omani workers in private sector

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: Portugal: New Segurança Social contribution model replaces self-filed DMR
entry.summary: Decreto-Lei 127/2025 of 9 December introduces a new model in which Segurança Social calculates the monthly declaration from data the employer communicates. The employer confirms or corrects it by the 20th of the following month (currently the 10th), silence counts as…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jan 2026 · Optional during 2026; mandatory 1 Jan 2027

Decreto-Lei 127/2025 of 9 December introduces a new model in which Segurança Social calculates the monthly declaration from data the employer communicates. The employer confirms or corrects it by the 20th of the following month (currently the 10th), silence counts as acceptance, and contributions are paid between the 1st and 25th of the following month. Changes to permanent pay must be communicated by the 10th of the following month via Segurança Social Direta or the Plataforma de Serviços de Interoperabilidade. Employers may opt in at any time during 2026; from 1 January 2027 the model is mandatory for all employers.

For the employer:

  • Once you opt in, the DMR can no longer be sent in the current format - plan the switch with your payroll provider.
  • Set up processes to communicate changes to permanent pay by the 10th of the following month, and to review the pre-calculated declaration by the 20th.
  • Prepare for mandatory use from 1 January 2027.

Source: Littler Portugal - Novo modelo de comunicação à Segurança Social

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.title: India: Four Labour Codes in force from 21 November 2025
entry.summary: The Code on Wages 2019, the Industrial Relations Code 2020, the Code on Social Security 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 took effect on 21 November 2025. They introduce a standardised definition of wages and extend gratuity to fixed-term…
entry.content:
In force, 21 Nov 2025

The Code on Wages 2019, the Industrial Relations Code 2020, the Code on Social Security 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 took effect on 21 November 2025. They introduce a standardised definition of wages and extend gratuity to fixed-term employees after one year of service (against five years for full-time employees).

For the employer:

  • Review salary structures and contracts against the new uniform definition of wages.
  • Provide gratuity to fixed-term employees who complete one year of service.
  • Watch for final central and state rules, which were yet to be notified.

Source: KPMG India - Implementation of labour codes: What changes and road ahead

entry.content:
In force, 2026 · Applies to 2026 wages

Government Regulation No. 49 of 2025 replaced the previous wage-setting framework after a Constitutional Court decision. The alpha coefficient used in the formula now ranges between 0.5 and 0.9, compared with the previous cap of 0.3, and sectoral minimum wages have been reintroduced in some regions.

For the employer:

  • Check the 2026 provincial (UMP) and regency/city (UMK) minimum wage decrees for each work location.
  • Check whether a sectoral minimum wage applies to your industry (for example construction, energy, high-tech manufacturing); it can exceed the standard UMP or UMK.

Source: RSM Indonesia - PP 49/2025 minimum wage regulation

entry.summary: This applies to federal government civil servants only and is not a private-sector payroll rule. By Office Memorandum dated 21 July 2026, the Ministry of Finance approved revised Basic Pay Scales and allowances effective 1 July 2026 for federal civil employees paid from civil…
entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

This applies to federal government civil servants only and is not a private-sector payroll rule. By Office Memorandum dated 21 July 2026, the Ministry of Finance approved revised Basic Pay Scales and allowances effective 1 July 2026 for federal civil employees paid from civil and defence estimates. BPS-2026 replaces BPS-2022 and merges the earlier ad-hoc relief allowances; a new Ad-hoc Relief Allowance-2026 of 7% of running basic pay applies from 1 July 2026 until further orders.

For the employer:

  • Federal payroll units: fix pay in BPS-2026 point to point from the stage held on 30 June 2026.
  • Stop the Ad-hoc Relief Allowances of 2022 (15%) and 2025 (10%), which cease on 1 July 2026, and pay the 7% allowance instead.
  • Annual increment remains admissible on 1 December each year.

Source: Government of Pakistan Ministry of Finance - Office Memorandum, Revision of Basic Pay Scales and Allowances of Civil Servants 2026

For information only, not legal or tax advice.

entry.content:
In force, 1 Jul 2026

The Finance Act 2026, enacted on 27 June 2026, reduced tax rates for salaried individuals in the First Schedule with effect from 1 July 2026. Income up to Rs 600,000 is untaxed, and the 35% rate now applies only to taxable income above Rs 7,000,000 (previously it applied from Rs 4,100,000).

For the employer:

  • Update salary withholding (section 149) to the new slabs: 1% over Rs 600,000; Rs 6,000 + 11% over Rs 1,200,000; Rs 116,000 + 20% over Rs 2,200,000; Rs 316,000 + 25% over Rs 3,200,000; Rs 541,000 + 29% over Rs 4,100,000; Rs 976,000 + 32% over Rs 5,600,000; Rs 1,424,000 + 35% over Rs 7,000,000.

Source: KPMG Taseer Hadi & Co. - A Brief of Finance Act, 2026 (July 2026)
